outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no result has been found that settles which classes of ODEs have Lyapunov's second method, in its classical or its 'canonically generalized' form, as a necessary and sufficient test for (asymptotic) stability. The window holds one new necessary-and-sufficient characterisation for a restricted class (switched nonlinear systems under average dwell-time, arXiv May 2024, ESAIM COCV 2025), a 2026 counterexample to a converse conjecture for homogeneous polynomial vector fields, a 2026 graded (decay-rate) converse characterisation, a 2025 survey, and several AI-learned Lyapunov-function papers that construct functions for particular systems and do not address the class question.
problem_asks: (1) Identify the classes of ODEs, describing dynamical systems, for which (2) Lyapunov's second method, in (2a) its classical form and (2b) its canonically generalized form, (3) gives necessary and sufficient conditions for (3a) stability of motion and, in the parenthetical '(asymptotical)', (3b) asymptotic stability of motion. The bullet asks for classes, not for one theorem: its answer is a list of classes plus, for each, the form of the method that is necessary and sufficient. It names no dimension, constant or particular system. Terms the bullet does not define: 'classes of ODEs' (no class is named), 'canonically generalized forms' (I could not locate this phrase in any source; see summary), and 'motion' (Russian-school phrasing, equivalent here to the state of an ODE system). The bullet's Wikipedia lead sentence, 'For certain classes of ODEs, the existence of Lyapunov functions is a necessary and sufficient condition for stability', is the only text I found that matches the bullet's shape.

events.what_happened: José Luis Massera, 'On Liapounoff's conditions of stability', Annals of Mathematics (2) 50(3), 705–721 (1949). Converse theorem: for an autonomous, continuously differentiable system with an asymptotically stable equilibrium, a Lyapunov function exists, built as a semi-infinite integral along solutions. Known to me from the Wikipedia Lyapunov function article (which cites this paper as its converse reference), the Wikipedia Massera's lemma page and the MacTutor publication list. I did not open the paper.
events.delivers: For autonomous, continuously differentiable systems with an asymptotically stable equilibrium: asymptotic stability implies that a Lyapunov function exists (converse direction). The class is autonomous and C1 with an equilibrium; the result is non-constructive, since the function is defined from the solutions.
events.remains: Time-varying systems, merely continuous right-hand sides and the canonically generalized form (Malkin 1954 and Kurzweil 1955–56 extend the converse; neither is covered here).
events.doubts: None specific. The statement is taken from secondary sources; the paper itself was not read.
events.direction: Cuts for the claim that a Lyapunov function characterises asymptotic stability for autonomous C1 systems.
events.object: The converse Lyapunov function is an integral along solutions, V(x) = integral over t from 0 to infinity of G(|phi(t,x)|) dt, with G a suitable function (per the search summary of the Wikipedia Massera's lemma page and Teel–Praly). Non-constructive: it is defined through the solutions themselves.

events.what_happened: Malkin (1954) observed that Massera's integral construction also yields a converse for time-varying systems, provided asymptotic stability and differentiability of f with respect to the state are uniform in time. Known only from a secondary account in the ESAIM COCV article of Teel and Praly (2000), seen in search. I did not open Malkin's paper or Teel–Praly.
events.delivers: Converse Lyapunov function for time-varying systems under uniform asymptotic stability with a class-KL bound on solutions for small initial data (per the search summary). Class: non-autonomous, C1 in the state, uniform in time.
events.remains: Non-uniform in time stability; continuous (non-differentiable) right-hand sides; the canonically generalized form.
events.doubts: Secondary account only. The uniformity hypothesis as stated is from the search summary, not from Malkin's paper.
events.direction: Cuts for the converse direction in the time-varying, uniform case.

events.what_happened: Kurzweil, 'On the inversion of Ljapunov's second theorem on stability of motion', Czechoslovak Mathematical Journal 6(2), 217–259 (1956), with a continuation in 6(4), 455–484, and a shorter note with the same title in 5(3), 435–438 (1955). Converse theorems for systems where the right-hand side is only continuous, so uniqueness of solutions is not assumed. Known from bibliographic records on the Czech digital library (dml.cz) and EuDML; the Russian text was not read.
events.delivers: Per secondary summaries: converse Lyapunov theorems for ODEs with continuous right-hand side, establishing that strong stability on an open neighbourhood, with a bounding function and a locally Lipschitz positive-definite function, implies a smooth converse Lyapunov function. The exact hypotheses were not read.
events.remains: Hypotheses and classes not confirmed from the paper; the canonically generalized form is not addressed.
events.doubts: The 1955 note may be a preliminary announcement; I did not check whether it contains the mathematics. Summary-level claims only.
events.direction: Cuts for the converse direction, under weaker regularity (continuous f).

events.what_happened: N. N. Krasovskii, 'On the inversion of theorems in the second method of A. M. Lyapunov for investigation of stability of motion', Uspekhi Matematicheskikh Nauk 11(3)(69), 159–164 (1956). Parallel to Kurzweil on the converse question. Known from a bibliographic record in search. I did not open it.
events.delivers: Unknown: the converse-theorem content was not read.
events.remains: Unknown from this source.
events.doubts: Not read; recorded because its title matches the converse question and the bullet's wording ('stability of motion').
events.direction: Unknown: not read.

events.what_happened: Zubov's method: the domain of attraction of an asymptotically stable equilibrium is characterised exactly by a transformed Lyapunov function W with 0 < W < 1 off the equilibrium, W tending to 1 at the boundary, and W satisfying a first-order PDE (the Zubov equation). Kellett's 2015 survey states this as an if-and-only-if characterisation (Theorem 5.1), and the Camilli–Grüne–Wirth survey (seen in search) covers it. I did not find the year of Zubov's original publication in any source I read.
events.delivers: A necessary and sufficient Lyapunov-type characterisation of the domain of attraction for a general nonlinear autonomous ODE (per Kellett's Theorem 5.1 as read in the ar5iv text). It characterises a domain, not stability as such.
events.remains: The bullet's question for classes of ODEs: Zubov's theorem is a general characterisation, but it is a characterisation of the domain of attraction, and it needs solving a PDE, which the sources note is a practical obstacle.
events.doubts: Date missing: the sources I read did not give Zubov's original year, and I did not guess one. Statement taken from Kellett's survey.
events.direction: Cuts for a necessary and sufficient Lyapunov-type characterisation of the stability region, for autonomous ODEs.
events.object: The transformed maximal Lyapunov function W in (0,1), whose 1-sublevel set is the domain of attraction (per Kellett and the Koopman/Zubov search summaries). Non-constructive in general: it is defined through the Zubov PDE.

events.what_happened: M. K. Sparavalo, 'The Lyapunov concept of stability from the standpoint of Poincaré approach: general procedure of utilization of Lyapunov functions for non-linear non-autonomous parametric differential inclusions', arXiv 1403.5761 (March 2014 per the arXiv identifier). The search summary says it argues that the Lyapunov second method gives only sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability, because Lyapunov functions cannot detect mosaic attractors in motion space, and proposes modifying the method or using a Poincaré-based approach. I read only the search summary, not the paper.
events.delivers: Per the search summary: a claim that the standard second method is sufficient but not necessary for asymptotic stability, and a proposal for remedies. Not a necessary-and-sufficient class result.
events.remains: Per the summary, the Poincaré approach is offered as an alternative. Whether it yields necessary and sufficient conditions for a class was not determined.
events.doubts: Summary-level only. The sufficiency-only claim is the author's own statement as summarised by search.
events.direction: Cuts against the standard second method being necessary as well as sufficient in general, per the author's own claim as summarised.
events.object: A mosaic-attractor example that the classical second method cannot detect (described in the search summary; not read).

events.what_happened: M. K. Sparavalo, 'Canonical Form of Lyapunov Second Method in Mathematical Modelling and Control Design', arXiv 2102.01737, submitted 2 February 2021, one version (12 pages). Introduces a canonical Lyapunov function, a canonizing diffeomorphism and a canonical form of dynamical systems, presented as a generalisation of the Lyapunov second method, linking ideas of Poincaré and Chetaev. Applied to tracking control of a thrust-vectored aircraft. The only source I found that uses 'canonical form' of the Lyapunov method; it is the closest match I found to 'canonically generalized' in the bullet, but the bullet's phrase is not confirmed as this paper's.
events.revisions: One version only (v1, 2 Feb 2021), per arXiv listing.
events.delivers: A generalised framework: a canonical Lyapunov function (positive definite diagonal quadratic form, per the search summary of the introduction) and canonizing transformations obtained via first integrals. The abstract claims no necessary-and-sufficient conditions for stability and no class characterisation; its stability claim is for the aircraft control law only.
events.remains: Whether the framework gives necessary and sufficient conditions for any class of ODEs: the abstract does not claim it.
events.doubts: Single arXiv preprint; no journal version or citing literature found. The author's 2016 self-published monograph (seen in search) is not read.
events.direction: Neutral on the bullet's necessity question: it presents a generalisation and makes no necessary-and-sufficient claim in the abstract.

events.what_happened: O. V. Druzhinina and A. A. Shestakov, 'Generalized direct Lyapunov method for the analysis of stability and attraction in general time systems', Sbornik: Mathematics 193(10), 1411–1441 (2002), DOI 10.1070/SM2002v193n10ABEH000684. Generalised Lyapunov functions relative to two filters, quasifilters or filter bases give necessary and sufficient conditions for stability and attraction, for general time systems in the senses of Birkhoff, Zubov and Seibert, systems with delay and input-output systems. Known from the Math-Net.ru abstract in search (the page itself refused connection, so I did not open it).
events.delivers: Per the abstract: necessary and sufficient conditions for stability and attraction, for the listed general time systems, under minimal structural assumptions, via generalised Lyapunov functions with respect to filters. This is the closest match I found to a 'generalized' form of the method with necessity and sufficiency.
events.remains: The classes in the bullet are ODEs; the listed systems are general time systems (filter-based), of which ODEs are at most a special case. Whether 'canonically generalized' refers to this framework was not confirmed.
events.doubts: Abstract only. Math-Net.ru lists it as cited by 5 papers; citing works not identified, so no later engagement is established.
events.direction: Cuts for necessary-and-sufficient conditions for stability in general time systems; it covers ODEs only as a special case if at all.

events.what_happened: A. R. Teel and L. Praly, ESAIM: Control, Optimisation and Calculus of Variations 5 (2000), 313–367 (numdam COCV_2000__5__313_0), 'A smooth Lyapunov function from a class-KL estimate involving two positive semidefinite functions'. A smooth converse Lyapunov function exists if and only if the class-KL estimate is robust for a perturbed differential inclusion; sufficient conditions are local Lipschitz continuity, or equal positive semidefinite functions with a backward completability condition. Known from the search abstract; I did not open the paper.
events.delivers: Per the search summary: a converse characterisation for differential inclusions, with an 'if and only if' robustness condition, and special cases that cover many converse theorems for ODEs. Authors leave open whether all class-KL estimates are robust.
events.remains: Whether every class-KL estimate is robust (stated open by the authors per the summary). The result is about inclusions, which contain ODEs as a special case.
events.doubts: Summary-level only.
events.direction: Cuts for converse Lyapunov results in the class-KL formulation, for differential inclusions with ODEs as a case.

events.what_happened: C. M. Kellett, 'Classical converse theorems in Lyapunov's second method', Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems Series B 20(8) (October 2015), arXiv 1502.04809 (v1 17 Feb 2015; v2 11 Aug 2016). A survey asking whether a given stability property implies the existence of an appropriate Lyapunov function, with the known answers collected. Read through the arXiv abstract and the ar5iv full text (the first 100k of 142k characters).
events.revisions: v1 17 Feb 2015; v2 11 Aug 2016 (current). Journal version DCDS-B 2015.
events.delivers: A survey, not a new theorem. Records necessary-and-sufficient statements by class: asymptotic stability of linear continuous-time (Thm 3.1) and linear discrete-time (Thm 3.2) systems; Zubov's characterisation of the domain of attraction (Thm 5.1); Barbashin–Krasovskii: a radially unbounded decrescent Lyapunov function is necessary and sufficient for uniform asymptotic stability in the large; robust strong KL-stability iff a smooth Lyapunov function exists (Thm 7.5 discrete, 7.6 continuous). Classes covered: autonomous and time-varying, continuous and discrete time, differential inclusions. The Lur'e result (Thm 4.1) is stated as not a converse theorem in the usual sense.
events.remains: A complete list of classes of ODEs for which the classical or generalised form is necessary and sufficient is not given in the survey; the bullet's classes are not enumerated in what I read. The survey does not discuss the 'canonically generalized' form.

checked_by.who: Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems Series B (journal of record)
checked_by.qualification: Peer-reviewed journal; the author is an established control theorist (Future Fellowship acknowledged in the paper)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the survey in 2015 (per arXiv journal reference)

events.doubts: None specific. The survey's own statements are its own summary of the literature, not new results.
events.direction: Surveys cases in which the converse holds (linear systems, Zubov's domain characterisation, uniform asymptotic stability in the large, robust KL with smooth Lyapunov functions). Cuts for the class-by-class necessary-and-sufficient reading of the bullet.

events.what_happened: Geiselhart, Gielen, Lazar and Wirth, 'An alternative converse Lyapunov theorem for discrete-time systems' (2013 preprint, per the search summary). Constructive converse theorem for discrete-time systems: existence of global Lyapunov functions for globally exponentially stable systems, and semi-global practical Lyapunov functions for globally asymptotically stable systems. Seen in search; not opened.
events.delivers: Per the search summary: converse theorems for discrete-time systems (not ODEs). Class: discrete-time, globally exponentially stable systems and globally asymptotically stable systems (practical).
events.remains: Not an ODE class; outside the bullet's classes by time domain.
events.doubts: Search summary only.
events.direction: Converse for discrete-time systems; discounted by class for the bullet's ODE question.

events.what_happened: A. A. Ahmadi and P. A. Parrilo, 'Converse results on existence of sum of squares Lyapunov functions', 50th IEEE CDC and European Control Conference (CDC-ECC 2011), Orlando, 12–15 December 2011, per the search summary. For homogeneous polynomial vector fields, if a polynomial Lyapunov function exists at any degree, a sum-of-squares Lyapunov function exists whose negative derivative is also SOS. Seen in search; not opened. The arXiv preprint 1201.2892 also appeared in search; I did not check whether it is the same paper.
events.revisions: A journal version (per search, 'later journal version ... planar systems ... switched linear systems', arXiv 1801.00070) followed; not read.
events.delivers: Per the search summary: a converse for polynomial Lyapunov functions for homogeneous polynomial vector fields, in the SOS-certificate sense. Class: homogeneous polynomial vector fields.
events.remains: Whether the converse holds at bounded degree (not, per Ahmadi and Parrilo 2013); general nonlinear ODE classes.
events.doubts: Search summary only. The relationship between the 2011 result and the arXiv 1201.2892 preprint is unchecked.
events.direction: Cuts for a converse in the polynomial-SOS class (homogeneous polynomial fields).

events.what_happened: A. A. Ahmadi and P. A. Parrilo, 'Stability of polynomial differential equations: complexity and converse Lyapunov questions', arXiv 1308.6833 (August 2013 per the identifier). Conjectures that asymptotic stability of a homogeneous polynomial vector field implies a polynomial Lyapunov function, and shows the minimum degree can be arbitrarily large even in fixed dimension and degree; also reports no monotonicity in degree. Seen in search; not opened.
events.delivers: Per the search summary: the conjecture (homogeneous asymptotic stability implies a polynomial Lyapunov function of some degree) and a degree-growth obstruction. Class: polynomial and homogeneous polynomial vector fields.
events.remains: The conjecture itself, which Liu and Fitzsimmons (2026) report disproved for the globally asymptotically stable case (see liu-fitzsimmons-2026).
events.doubts: Search summary only; the conjecture is recorded as stated in the 2026 Liu and Fitzsimmons abstract and in search.
events.direction: Conjectures a converse for homogeneous polynomial vector fields.

events.what_happened: P. Pepe and I. Karafyllis, arXiv 1206.3504 (June 2012 per identifier). For time-invariant neutral functional differential equations in Hale's form, existence of a Lyapunov–Krasovskii functional is necessary and sufficient for uniform global asymptotic stability and global exponential stability. Seen in search; not opened.
events.delivers: Per the search summary: a necessary-and-sufficient converse for neutral functional differential equations (delay, not ODEs). Class: neutral FDEs in Hale's form.
events.remains: Not an ODE class.
events.doubts: Search summary only.
events.direction: Converse for delay systems; discounted by class for the bullet's ODE question.

events.what_happened: A. Mironchenko and F. Wirth, 'Non-coercive Lyapunov functions for infinite-dimensional systems', arXiv 1612.06575 (posted 20 Dec 2016), published Journal of Differential Equations 266 (2019), 7038–7072. Non-coercive Lyapunov functions for infinite-dimensional systems with disturbances; converse theorems for non-coercive functions, with examples showing assumptions are needed. Seen in search; not opened.
events.delivers: Per the search summary: sufficiency of non-coercive Lyapunov functions for uniform global asymptotic stability of infinite-dimensional systems under a mild extra assumption, plus converse theorems. Class: infinite-dimensional systems.
events.remains: Not an ODE class.
events.doubts: Search summary only.
events.direction: Converse for infinite-dimensional systems; discounted by class for the bullet's ODE question.

events.what_happened: E. D. Sontag and Y. Wang, arXiv math/9902024 (February 1999 per identifier): necessary and sufficient Lyapunov-type characterisations of several notions of input-to-output stability. Seen in search; not opened.
events.delivers: Per the search summary: necessary and sufficient characterisations of input-to-output stability notions, not of stability of motion for an unforced ODE.
events.remains: Not the bullet's notion.
events.doubts: Search summary only. Recorded as a different notion (input-to-output stability).
events.direction: Different property; not a stability-of-motion class result.

events.what_happened: M. Della Rossa and A. Tanwani, 'Converse Lyapunov results for stability of switched systems with average dwell-time', arXiv 2405.03560 (v1 posted 6 May 2024; v2 7 Jan 2025), published ESAIM: COCV 31 (2025), article 15, DOI 10.1051/cocv/2025006 (received 18 April 2024, accepted 2 January 2025, online 18 February 2025). Gives necessary and sufficient conditions, built from multiple Lyapunov functions, characterising stability of switched nonlinear systems under average dwell-time constraints; the linear switched case is a corollary. A counterexample shows that a dwell-time lower bound need not give stability under an average dwell-time with the same bound. Read from the arXiv abstract page (and the arXiv listing and journal page in search); full text not read.
events.revisions: v1 6 May 2024; v2 7 Jan 2025. Journal: ESAIM COCV 31 (2025) 15, accepted 2 Jan 2025, online 18 Feb 2025.
events.delivers: A necessary and sufficient characterisation of stability (the abstract does not say asymptotic stability) for switched nonlinear systems under average dwell-time switching, in terms of multiple Lyapunov functions, with inequalities that do not depend on subsystem flows. The linear switched systems case is a corollary. Class: switched nonlinear systems (ODE-type subsystems) with average dwell-time switching.
events.remains: The bullet's classes of ODEs in the classical single-Lyapunov-function form: this is a multiple-Lyapunov-function characterisation for a switched class, and it is not a classical single-function result. Whether the multiple-function form counts as the bullet's 'canonically generalized' form is the judging pass's call.

events.what_happened: Jie Feng, Haohan Zou and Yuanyuan Shi, 'Combining neural networks and symbolic regression for analytical Lyapunov function discovery' (CoNSAL), arXiv 2406.15675, v1 21 June 2024, v3 12 July 2024; workshop paper at the ICML 2024 Workshop on Foundations of Reinforcement Learning and Control. Trains a neural Lyapunov function and distils it by symbolic regression into an analytical form, searching for counterexamples; tested on 2-D inverted pendulum, path following, Van der Pol, 3-D trig dynamics, a 4-D rotating-wheel pendulum and a 6-D three-bus power system. Read from the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: Constructs analytical Lyapunov functions for named example systems. It establishes no characterisation of a class and no necessary-and-sufficient condition.
events.remains: All of the bullet's question: the work is about finding certificates for particular systems.
events.directly_checkable: Each example's Lyapunov function can be checked by substitution into the Lie derivative condition, per the method's own verification step (not checked by me).
events.doubts: Different question: a construction for specific systems, not a class result. Verification is by the authors' method and its checks, not an independent reading.
events.direction: Neutral to the classes question; finds certificates for specific systems.
events.object: Analytical Lyapunov functions for the listed example systems (the specific formulas are not in the abstract I read). The object is a certificate for each example, not a counterexample to any class claim.

systems.name: neural Lyapunov function (neural network trained by the authors, with symbolic regression)
systems.what_it_did: Trains a neural network as a candidate Lyapunov function, then symbolic regression distils it into an analytical formula; the output is an analytical Lyapunov function for each example.
systems.basis_quote: symbolic regression is applied to distill the neural network to precise analytical forms (per the fetch summary of the abstract; not verbatim-checked)

events.what_happened: Alberto Alfarano, François Charton and Amaury Hayat, 'Global Lyapunov functions: a long-standing open problem in mathematics, with symbolic transformers', arXiv 2410.08304 (submitted 10 October 2024, v1 only), NeurIPS 2024. An earlier version, 'Discovering Lyapunov functions with transformers', is a 2023 NeurIPS (workshop) paper, predating the window. The paper trains sequence-to-sequence transformers on synthetic data built from random solutions to find global Lyapunov functions. Its abstract says they perform better than algorithmic solvers and humans on polynomial systems and can discover new Lyapunov functions for non-polynomial systems. Read from the arXiv abstract page.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv (10 Oct 2024). The 2023 version 'Discovering Lyapunov functions with transformers' is an earlier, pre-window version of the same line of work.
events.delivers: Finds global Lyapunov functions for particular polynomial and non-polynomial systems using the authors' transformers. Establishes no class characterisation and no necessary-and-sufficient condition. The abstract frames global Lyapunov function finding as the open problem.
events.remains: The bullet's question about classes of ODEs for which the method is necessary and sufficient: unaddressed by this paper.

checked_by.qualification: Conference peer review of the NeurIPS 2024 paper
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted to NeurIPS 2024 (per the NeurIPS proceedings listing in search)

Reported to be a human-versus-model comparison on polynomial systems (per the abstract and a secondary Japanese news report in search, not read). A secondary write-up overstates it as solving a 132-year-old problem; the paper itself describes the problem as still lacking a general solution.
events.direction: Neutral to the classes question; discovers functions for particular systems.
events.object: New Lyapunov functions for non-polynomial systems (the systems and functions are not specified in the abstract I read). The candidate functions are found by the transformers and presumably checked symbolically; the abstract does not say.

events.what_happened: Haohan Zou, Jie Feng, Hao Zhao and Yuanyuan Shi, 'Analytical Lyapunov Function Discovery: An RL-based Generative Approach', arXiv 2502.02014 (v1 4 Feb 2025; v2 11 Feb 2025; v3 4 Jun 2025), ICML 2025 (PMLR 267). A transformer generates candidate analytical local Lyapunov functions; a falsifier checks them and the trainer is refined by a risk-seeking policy gradient; formal verification performs the final check. Reports local functions for systems up to ten dimensions, including some not previously in the control literature (per the abstract). Read from the arXiv abstract page.

events.what_happened: Ihab Haidar and Paolo Mason, 'Converse Lyapunov results for uniform stability properties', Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications 206(2) (August 2025), DOI 10.1007/s10957-025-02698-1. A survey of converse Lyapunov results for uniform asymptotic stability under parametric perturbations, with emphasis on infinite-dimensional systems. The Springer page redirected to an identity-provider login and was not opened; the abstract was read via the RePEc/IDEAS record in search. No arXiv version found.

Emphasis on uniform asymptotic stability with parametric perturbations and on infinite-dimensional systems.

events.what_happened: M. A. Novikov, 'On conventional stability of steady-state motions of mechanical systems with a partial Steklov integral', Mechanics of Solids 60(6), 4390–4399 (2025), DOI 10.1134/S0025654425601259 (received 18 March 2025, revised 27 May 2025, accepted 28 May 2025). Uses Chetaev's technique with a Lyapunov function built from a full set of first integrals of the perturbed motion, to obtain sufficient conditions 'the most close to the necessary conditions' for stability of steady-state motions. Read from the journal abstract page.

events.what_happened: Jun Liu and Maxwell Fitzsimmons, 'A globally asymptotically stable planar homogeneous polynomial vector field with no polynomial Lyapunov function', arXiv 2607.16171 (v1 submitted 17 July 2026; one version). Disproves the conjecture that every globally asymptotically stable homogeneous polynomial vector field admits a homogeneous polynomial Lyapunov function, with a planar homogeneous cubic with integer coefficients. The abstract also claims a machine-checked Lean 4 formalisation of the main result, with no URL in the abstract I read. Read from the arXiv abstract page; the full text was not read.
events.revisions: One version (v1, 17 Jul 2026), per arXiv listing.
events.delivers: For the class of planar homogeneous cubic polynomial vector fields with integer coefficients: a globally asymptotically stable field with no homogeneous polynomial Lyapunov function (with nonpositive Lie derivative) and no real-analytic Lyapunov function even locally. The same field has an explicit degree-two homogeneous Lyapunov function that is radially unbounded and C1 everywhere, smooth away from the origin. Restriction: planar, homogeneous, cubic, integer coefficients, and only polynomial/homogeneous and real-analytic Lyapunov functions are excluded; the smooth non-polynomial Lyapunov function that exists is not excluded.
events.remains: Whether the bullet's classical or generalised Lyapunov forms are necessary and sufficient for asymptotic stability for the classes in question: the result shows a polynomial/homogeneous class is not characterised by polynomial Lyapunov functions, and says nothing about the non-polynomial converse, which the explicit C1 function suggests exists.

The abstract states 'real-analytic Lyapunov function' non-existence; the full proof was not read. No AI involvement is disclosed in the abstract.

It admits no homogeneous polynomial Lyapunov function with nonpositive Lie derivative and no real-analytic Lyapunov function even locally. It does admit an explicit degree-two homogeneous Lyapunov function that is radially unbounded, C1 everywhere and smooth away from the origin. Explicit: yes; the non-existence claims are proofs (formalised in Lean 4 per the abstract), not constructions.

events.what_happened: Ben Cassie, 'Lyapunov-odes-lean: formal proofs of Lyapunov stability theorems for autonomous ODEs in Lean 4', Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20475912, published 31 May 2026 (v1). Lean 4 / Mathlib library: solutions of x' = f(x) via HasDerivAt, Lyapunov and asymptotic stability at the origin, exponential decay via Mathlib's Gronwall inequality. The description claims zero sorry and zero admit; the LaSalle convergence step is an explicit hypothesis. Repository at github.com/velvetmonkey/lyapunov-odes-lean (MIT). I read the Zenodo description only; I did not open the repository.

events.what_happened: Yigit Narter and Inigo Incer, 'On a gradation for asymptotic stability', arXiv 2609.03120 (eess.SY; v1 2 September 2026, v2 11 September 2026). Introduces graded asymptotic stability: degree zero is exponential stability, and degree m > 0 is algebraic decay of order t^(-1/m). Gives direct and converse Lyapunov characterisations for admissible degrees, and conditions for certifying the exact degree; examples include Hopf, Bautin, fractional-degree and time-varying systems. Read from the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: Direct and converse Lyapunov characterisations for each admissible degree of a refined asymptotic stability (decay rate). For degree zero this is an exponential-stability characterisation. The asymptotic stability of the bullet is the union over degrees, so this is a stronger, refined notion: a characterisation of decay rate, not of asymptotic stability as such (on the abstract's wording).
events.remains: The bullet's classes of ODEs for asymptotic stability as such: the abstract does not restate the classical converse as a class result. Whether 'converse Lyapunov characterisations for admissible degrees' are necessary and sufficient is not stated in the abstract.
events.doubts: The abstract does not say 'necessary and sufficient'; that is an inference. Full text not read. Two-version preprint; v2 changes not read.
events.direction: A refined (stronger) notion of asymptotic stability: converse characterisations per decay degree. Cuts for converse characterisations of graded stability; does not settle the classical question as stated.

disputes.summary: No priority dispute found for the classical converse results. For the 2024–2026 items, the authors of the switched-system, polynomial and graded results are distinct, and I found no claim of an earlier proof of the same statement.

summary: The bullet asks for the classes of ODEs in which Lyapunov's second method, classical or canonically generalised, is necessary and sufficient for (asymptotic) stability. The Wikipedia Lyapunov function article, which the bullet links to, says that for certain classes of ODEs the existence of Lyapunov functions is necessary and sufficient for stability and cites Massera (1949) as the converse, but it does not name the classes. The classical answer is therefore spread across the converse literature: Massera (1949) for autonomous C1 systems, Malkin (1954) and Kurzweil (1955–56) for time-varying and continuous systems, Barbashin–Krasovskii for uniform asymptotic stability in the large, and linear systems, as collected in Kellett's 2015 survey (arXiv 1502.04809, read through the first 100k of about 142k characters of the ar5iv text). Those are pre-window and I have recorded them as events. Within the window (after 26 January 2024), the closest match to a new necessary-and-sufficient characterisation is Della Rossa and Tanwani (arXiv 2405.03560, first posted 6 May 2024; ESAIM COCV 2025). It gives such conditions for switched nonlinear systems under average dwell-time constraints, using multiple Lyapunov functions. Whether that counts as the bullet's 'canonically generalized' form, and whether it is a class of ODEs in the bullet's sense, is the call I could not make. Other in-window items are: a 2026 counterexample by Liu and Fitzsimmons (arXiv 2607.16171, 17 July 2026) showing that a globally asymptotically stable planar homogeneous cubic has no homogeneous polynomial, or real-analytic, Lyapunov function, though it has an explicit smooth one away from the origin; a 2026 graded converse characterisation by Narter and Incer (arXiv 2609.03120), which concerns decay-rate degrees rather than asymptotic stability as such; a 2025 Mechanics of Solids paper by Novikov that gets sufficient conditions 'the most close to' necessary for one mechanical system, not an exact result; and a 2025 JOTA survey by Haidar and Mason on converse results for uniform stability (read only from its abstract, since the Springer page redirected to a login). The AI-related items (Alfarano, Charton and Hayat 2024; Feng, Zou and Shi 2024; Zou et al. 2025; Serry et al. 2025; Lalik 2024; a 2025 PINN preprint; a 2026 Komputika overview) all find or approximate Lyapunov functions for particular systems or for discrete-time systems. None establishes a class characterisation, so each carries the different-question tag in its record. Where a call was close, both readings are in the events. The 'canonically generalized' phrase is not found in any source I read. The closest candidates are Sparavalo (arXiv 2102.01737, 2021, 'canonical form of the Lyapunov second method', which claims no necessary-and-sufficient conditions) and Druzhinina and Shestakov (2002, 'generalized direct Lyapunov method', which claims necessary and sufficient conditions for general time systems). Neither matches the bullet's wording. I read most of the in-window source abstracts but only a few full texts, and WebFetch returns model-summarised page content, so quoted sentences are as the fetch tool returned them and were not checked against the originals. No AI system is credited with a classification, a converse or a necessary-and-sufficient condition anywhere in the window. Where a system was named (transformers, a neural Lyapunov function, a physics-informed network), its role was to construct or approximate a Lyapunov function for named examples.
competing_reading: One reading takes the bullet to be answered already: the classical converses (Massera, Malkin, Kurzweil, Barbashin–Krasovskii, Zubov, and the linear case in Kellett's survey) identify the classes in which Lyapunov functions are necessary and sufficient, so the bullet is settled by pre-window results and nothing in the window changes it. A second reading takes the bullet's 'canonically generalized forms' as a request for a specific framework (for example Druzhinina–Shestakov's filter-based method, or Sparavalo's canonical form), and in that reading the window's Della Rossa–Tanwani multiple-function characterisation may count as a generalised form, adding a class; a third reading asks for a list of classes as a whole, which no source I found provides, so the question stays open on that reading. Within the window, the Liu–Fitzsimmons counterexample can be read as cutting against a polynomial-class converse, or as irrelevant because the explicit smooth Lyapunov function it exhibits is consistent with the classical converse.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The source of the bullet's phrase 'canonically generalized forms': if it names Sparavalo's canonical form or Druzhinina–Shestakov's generalised method, the relevant framework and its necessary-and-sufficient claims can be checked directly; the Wikipedia bullet has no citation attached (confirmed on the list page). (2) The full text of Della Rossa and Tanwani: whether the stability notion is asymptotic, and whether the class is ODE-type; the journal PDF at the DOI. (3) The full text of Liu and Fitzsimmons and their Lean repository: the exact field, the non-existence proofs, and whether the Lean code is sorry-free. (4) The Massera, Malkin, Kurzweil and Kellett papers read in full, to fix the classes in the pre-window classical answer. (5) Whether any source names the class list the Wikipedia lead refers to ('for certain classes of ODEs'); the Wikipedia article history would show whether that sentence was added after January 2024.

event.what_happened: M. Della Rossa and A. Tanwani, 'Converse Lyapunov results for stability of switched systems with average dwell-time', arXiv 2405.03560 (v1 posted 6 May 2024; v2 7 Jan 2025), published ESAIM: COCV 31 (2025), article 15, DOI 10.1051/cocv/2025006 (received 18 April 2024, accepted 2 January 2025, online 18 February 2025). Gives necessary and sufficient conditions, built from multiple Lyapunov functions, characterising stability of switched nonlinear systems under average dwell-time constraints; the linear switched case is a corollary. A counterexample shows that a dwell-time lower bound need not give stability under an average dwell-time with the same bound. Read from the arXiv abstract page (and the arXiv listing and journal page in search); full text not read.
event.revisions: v1 6 May 2024; v2 7 Jan 2025. Journal: ESAIM COCV 31 (2025) 15, accepted 2 Jan 2025, online 18 Feb 2025.
event.delivers: A necessary and sufficient characterisation of stability (the abstract does not say asymptotic stability) for switched nonlinear systems under average dwell-time switching, in terms of multiple Lyapunov functions, with inequalities that do not depend on subsystem flows. The linear switched systems case is a corollary. Class: switched nonlinear systems (ODE-type subsystems) with average dwell-time switching.
event.remains: The bullet's classes of ODEs in the classical single-Lyapunov-function form: this is a multiple-Lyapunov-function characterisation for a switched class, and it is not a classical single-function result. Whether the multiple-function form counts as the bullet's 'canonically generalized' form is the judging pass's call.

judgement.why: The statement asks for the classes of ODEs on which Lyapunov's second method, classical or generalised, is necessary and sufficient for (asymptotic) stability, so each converse theorem for a named class answers one restriction and is a case. The classical converses (Massera, Malkin, Kurzweil, Teel–Praly, Zubov) are pre-snapshot cases. The close call is Della Rossa–Tanwani (2024, ESAIM COCV): a necessary-and-sufficient multiple-Lyapunov-function characterisation for switched nonlinear systems under average dwell-time. Switched systems are piecewise-defined ODEs, and multiple Lyapunov functions are a standard generalised form of the method, so I counted it as a case rather than a variant; journal acceptance counts as digested. Liu–Fitzsimmons 2026 refutes a conjecture about polynomial Lyapunov functions, and it exhibits a smooth Lyapunov function for the same field, so on the statement's question it is a variant. Narter–Incer concerns a graded, stronger notion of stability, so it is also a variant. The AI papers construct Lyapunov functions for particular systems, so their scope is none. On their own quotes the trained models produced those functions, which makes their role generated, but none of these events bears on the class question. Lalik's and Serry's networks only estimate or approximate, so their role is none. Lalik's January 2024 month and Lai–Motta's bare year 2024 cannot be placed either side of 26 January.
judgement.doubts: The phrase 'canonically generalized forms' is unsourced. If it excludes multiple-Lyapunov-function frameworks or switched systems, Della Rossa–Tanwani becomes a variant and nothing after the snapshot survives. Zubov's date is missing. Several pre-snapshot verifications rest on journal publication known only from secondary summaries.
